Can privacy be preserved 2 bringing safety and security to a world that seems increasingly 3 ? items.text:
The EU is faced with so many problems that ____
A. it has more or less lost faith in markets.
B. even its supporters begin to feel concerned.
C. some of its member countries plan to abandon euro.
D. it intends to deny the possibility of devaluation.
items.passage: Will the European Union make it? The question would have sounded strange not long ago. Now even the project’s greatest cheerleaders talk of a continent facing a “Bermuda triangle” of debt, population decline and lower growth. As well as those chronic problems, the EU faces an acute crisis in its economic core, the 16 countries that use the single currency. Markets have lost faith that the euro zone’s economies, weaker or stronger, will one day converge thanks to the discipline of sharing a single currency, which denies uncompetitive members the quick fix of devaluation. Yet the debate about how to save Europe’s single currency from disintegration is stuck. It is stuck because the euro zone’s dominant powers, France and Germany, agree on the need for greater harmonisation within the euro zone, but disagree about what to harmonise. Germany thinks the euro must be saved by stricter rules on borrowing, spending and competitiveness, backed by quasi-automatic sanctions for governments that do not obey. These might include threats to freeze EU funds for poorer regions and EU mega-projects, and even the suspension of a country’s voting rights in EU ministerial councils. It insists that economic co-ordination should involve all 27 members of the EU club, among whom there is a small majority for free-market liberalism and economic rigour; in the inner core alone, Germany fears, a small majority favour French interference. A “southern” camp headed by French wants something different: “European economic government” within an inner core of euro-zone members. Translated, that means politicians intervening in monetary policy and a system of redistribution from richer to poorer members, via cheaper borrowing for governments through common Eurobonds or complete fiscal transfers. Finally, figures close to the French government have murmured, euro-zone members should agree to some fiscal and social harmonisation: eg., curbing competition in corporate-tax rates or labour costs. It is too soon to write off the EU. It remains the world’s largest trading block. At its best, the European project is remarkably liberal: built around a single market of 27 rich and poor countries, its internal borders are far more open to goods, capital and labour than any comparable trading area. It is an ambitious attempt to blunt the sharpest edges of globalisation, and make capitalism benign.

将 Andrew Lansley held that 与对应选项匹配。
A. “fat taxes” should be imposed on fast-food producers such as McDonald’s.
B. the government should ban fast-food outlets in the neighborhood of schools.
C. “lecturing” was an effective way to improve school lunches in England.
D. cigarette-style warnings should be introduced to children about the dangers of a poor diet.
E. the producers of crisps and candies could contribute significantly to the Change4Life campaign.
F. parents should set good examples for their children by keeping a healthy diet at home.
G. the government should strengthen the sense of responsibility among businesses.
items.passage: Leading doctors today weigh in on the debate over the government’s role in promoting public health by demanding that ministers impose “fat taxes” on unhealthy food and introduce cigarette-style warnings to children about the dangers of a poor diet. The demands follow comments made last week by the health secretary, Andrew Lansley, who insisted the government could not force people to make healthy choices and promised to free businesses from public health regulations. But senior medical figures want to stop fast-food outlets opening near schools, restrict advertising of products high in fat, salt or sugar, and limit sponsorship of sports events by fast-food producers such as McDonald’s. They argue that government action is necessary to curb Britain’s addiction to unhealthy food and help halt spiraling rates of obesity, diabetes and heart disease. Professor Terence Stephenson, president of the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health, said that the consumption of unhealthy food should be seen to be just as damaging as smoking or excessive drinking. “Thirty years ago, it would have been inconceivable to have imagined a ban on smoking in the workplace or in pubs, and yet that is what we have now. Are we willing to be just as courageous in respect of obesity? I would suggest that we should be,” said the leader of the UK’s children’s doctors. Lansley has alarmed health campaigners by suggesting he wants industry rather than government to take the lead. He said that manufacturers of crisps and candies could play a central role in the Change4Life campaign, the centrepiece of government efforts to boost healthy eating and fitness. He has also criticised the celebrity chef Jamie Oliver’s high-profile attempt to improve school lunches in England as an example of how “lecturing” people was not the best way to change their behaviour. Stephenson suggested potential restrictions could include banning TV advertisements for foods high in fat, salt or sugar before 9 pm and limiting them on billboards or in cinemas. “If we were really bold, we might even begin to think of high-calorie fast food in the same way as cigarettes — by setting strict limits on advertising, product placement and sponsorship of sports events,” he said. Such a move could affect firms such as McDonald’s, which sponsors the youth coaching scheme run by Football Association. Fast-food chains should also stop offering “inducements” such as toys, cute animals and mobile phone credit to lure young customers, Stephenson said. Professor Dinesh Bhugra, president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists, said: “If children are taught about the impact that food has on their growth, and that some things can harm, at least information is available up front.” He also urged councils to impose “fast-food-free zones” around schools and hospitals — areas within which takeaways cannot open. A Department of Health spokesperson said: “We need to create a new vision for public health where all of society works together to get healthy and live longer. This includes creating a new ‘responsibility deal’ with business, built on social responsibility, not state regulation. Later this year, we will publish a white paper setting out exactly how we will achieve this.” The food industry will be alarmed that such senior doctors back such radical moves, especially the call to use some of the tough tactics that have been deployed against smoking over the last decade.

Professor Dinesh Bhugra, president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists, said: “If children are taught about the impact that food has on their growth, and that some things can harm, at least information is available up front.” He also urged councils to impose “fast-food-free zones” around schools and hospitals — areas within which takeaways cannot open. A Department of Health spokesperson said: “We need to create a new vision for public health where all of society works together to get healthy and live longer. This includes creating a new ‘responsibility deal’ with business, built on social responsibility, not state regulation. Later this year, we will publish a white paper setting out exactly how we will achieve this.” The food industry will be alarmed that such senior doctors back such radical moves, especially the call to use some of the tough tactics that have been deployed against smoking over the last decade.
steps: 考点：多项对应（信息匹配），定位卫生部发言人关于 responsibility deal 的表述。
原文定位："This includes creating a new 'responsibility deal' with business, built on social responsibility, not state regulation." 发言人主张与企业建立以社会责任为基础的"责任协议"，而非靠国家立法强制。
这对应 G（the government should strengthen the sense of responsibility among businesses）。A、B、D 都是医生要求的税收、禁令与警告，与发言人 not state regulation 的立场相反；E 是 Lansley 的具体观点；C、F 与该发言无关。

items.chapterTitle: 英语二 2011 真题（整理版）
items.source: 2011 年全国硕士研究生招生考试 英语（二）题目整理版
items.text:
请将下列英文段落译成中文。
Who would have thought that, globally, the IT industry produces about the same volume of greenhouse gases as the world’s airlines do — roughly 2 percent of all CO₂ emissions? Many everyday tasks take a surprising toll on the environment. A Google search can leak between 0.2 and 7.0 grams of CO₂, depending on how many attempts are needed to get the “right” answer. To deliver results to its users quickly, then, Google has to maintain vast data centres around the world, packed with powerful computers. While producing large quantities of CO₂, these computers emit a great deal of heat, so the centres need to be well air- conditioned, which uses even more energy. However, Google and other big tech providers monitor their efficiency closely and make improvements. Monitoring is the first step on the road to reduction, but there is much more to be done, and not just by big companies.
items.answer: 有谁会想到，在全球范围内，IT 行业产生的温室气体总量与世界各航空公司的大致相当——约占全部二氧化碳排放量的 2%。许多日常工作都对环境造成了惊人的破坏。一次谷歌搜索会排放 0.2 克到 7.0 克二氧化碳，具体数值取决于为了得到"正确答案"需要尝试多少次。为了迅速地把搜索结果呈送给用户，谷歌必须在世界各地维护庞大的数据中心，里面装满了功能强大的计算机。这些计算机在产生大量二氧化碳的同时，还散发着大量热量，因此数据中心需要良好的空调降温，而这又要消耗更多能源。不过，谷歌和其他大型技术供应商会密切监控自身的能效，并不断作出改进。监控仅仅是走上减排之路的第一步，需要做的事情还有很多，而且要做这些事的不只是大公司。
steps: 考点：英译汉翻译——反问句气、长句切分与术语数字的准确转换（15 分）。
首句 Who would have thought that... 是反问句，要译出"有谁会想到"的惊讶语气；roughly 2 percent of all CO2 emissions 译为"约占全部二氧化碳排放量的 2%"，数字与百分比不可漏译错译。
A Google search can leak... 一句中 leak 取引申义"排放"；depending on how many attempts are needed... 是条件状语，译为"取决于为了得到正确答案需要尝试多少次"，不要逐字硬译。

To deliver results... 长句按意群切分：目的状语提前，maintain vast data centres 译"维护庞大的数据中心"；While producing large quantities of CO2, these computers emit a great deal of heat 与 so the centres need to be well air-conditioned 的因果链要衔接顺畅。
末句 Monitoring is the first step on the road to reduction 可译为"监控是走向减排的第一步"；and not just by big companies 是省略结构，补全为"要做这些事的不只是大公司"，避免句子残缺。

items.text: Suppose your cousin Li Ming has just been admitted to a university. Write him/her a letter to 1) congratulate him/her, and 2) give him/her suggestions on how to get prepared for university life. You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not sign your own name at the end of the letter. Use “Zhang Wei” instead. Do not write the address. (10 points)
items.answer:
Dear Li Ming,

Congratulations on your admission to the university! I was truly delighted to hear the good news, and I believe you will have a wonderful time in the coming four years.

To get well prepared for university life, I would like to give you a few suggestions. First, try to develop the ability to study independently, because at university no teacher will push you as closely as in high school. Second, learn to manage your time and money wisely, and take an active part in student societies, where you can make new friends and gain valuable experience. Finally, keep a healthy lifestyle by doing sports regularly.

I wish you every success in your university life.

Yours,
Zhang Wei
steps: 考点：应用文写作——祝贺信与建议信的复合功能（小作文 10 分，约 100 词）。
结构分三部分：第一段点明写信目的并表达祝贺（Congratulations on your admission to...）；第二段用 First、Second、Finally 分层给出建议——培养自主学习能力、合理管理时间与金钱、参加社团、坚持锻炼；第三段以祝愿收尾。
格式与硬性要求：称呼 Dear Li Ming，落款必须按题目要求使用 Zhang Wei，不得签自己的真实姓名，也不要写地址，缺一即扣分。
语言得分点：be admitted to、get prepared for、take an active part in、manage your time and money wisely 等地道搭配；全文约 105 词，符合约 100 词的要求。

items.chapterTitle: 英语二 2011 真题（整理版）
items.source: 2011 年全国硕士研究生招生考试 英语（二）题目整理版
items.text: Write an essay based on the following chart. In your writing, you should 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You should write at least 150 words. Write your essay on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
items.answer:
The bar chart clearly shows the changes in the market shares of three types of cars in China in 2008 and 2009.

As can be seen from the chart, Chinese brands gained considerable ground during this period: their market share rose from about 25% in 2008 to roughly 33% in 2009. In sharp contrast, Japanese brands lost their leading position, with their share dropping from about 35% to around 25%. The American brands, whose share was the smallest of the three, remained almost unchanged at a little over 10%.

Several factors may account for these changes. To begin with, Chinese car makers have made remarkable progress in quality and technology while keeping their prices comparatively low, which makes domestic cars increasingly attractive to ordinary buyers. Moreover, favorable government policies, such as the purchase-tax reduction for small-displacement cars, have strongly boosted the sales of Chinese brands, most of which fall into this category.

In my opinion, the rise of Chinese brands is an encouraging sign of the growing strength of China's automobile industry. If domestic manufacturers continue to improve their technology and brand image, they are likely to win an even larger share of the market in the years to come.
steps: 考点：图表作文——柱状图的数据描述加原因分析与评论（大作文 15 分，至少 150 词）。
第一段总述图表主题：2008 与 2009 两年中国轿车市场国产品牌、日系品牌、美系品牌市场份额的变化；图表具体数值以原卷图片为准，行文中用 about、roughly 等约数表述。
第二段逐一描述趋势并作对比：国产品牌份额明显上升（约 25%→33%），日系品牌明显下降（约 35%→25%），美系品牌基本稳定（略高于 10%），善用 in sharp contrast、remained almost unchanged 等对比与趋势句型。
第三段分析原因：国产车质量与技术进步、价格相对低廉，以及小排量汽车购置税优惠等政策扶持；最后一段给出评论与展望：国产品牌崛起是中国汽车工业实力增强的信号，未来份额有望继续扩大。全文约 200 词，满足字数要求。
